text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- CENBANK DENOUNCES $1.4 BLN EXCHANGE FRAUD

The Central Bank has denounced instances of foreign exchange fraud and money laundering amounting to $1.4 billion by account holders of banks in collusion with Banco do Brasil staff and employees from various state banks.
-- TRADE BALANCE SHOWS $4 BLN DEFICIT UNTIL APRIL
Brazil's April trade balance shows a deficit of $951 million, bringing the total trade gap in the four months to the end of April to $4 billion.
-- CVRD AUCTION REMAINS SUSPENDED INDEFINITELY
The privatization auction of mining giant CVRD remains suspended, as the government awaits a court ruling on its appeal which aims to get rid of all injunctions against the auction in one sweep.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- HIGHER TAX HITS CAR BUSINESS
Last week's increase in the financial transaction tax to 15 percent from 6 percent paralyzed car sales paid for in installments.
-- FOUR PEOPLE KILLED, 17 INJURED IN CAR ACCIDENTS

Four people were killed and six were injured in a Rio de Janeiro shantytown when the driver of a car lost control and ran over people standing on a sidewalk. In a similar accident in Sao Paulo, 11 people were run over and injured by a car.
O GLOBO
-- CARDOSO MOBILIZES CONGRESSIONAL LEADERS FOR REFORM VOTE
The government is mobilizing its congressional leaders to guarantee favorable votes on its civil service reform bill.
-- DELAY IN CVRD AUCTION IRRITATES BUYER CANDIDATES

The leader of one of the consortia planning to bid in the privatization auction of mining giant CVRD, Antonio Ermirio de Moraes, says he and his Valecom partners are irritated with the delay of the auction.
-- TELEPHONES TO COST 300 REAIS AS OF TODAY
Telephone installations will cost 300 reais as of today, but in cities like Rio and Sao Paulo where there are huge waiting lines people could be waiting a long time for their installations.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom 5521 5074151))
